title: Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models
knob_name: noise std sigma on all parameters, swept 0 to 0.01 step 1e-4
base_model: Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-70B, Mistral-7B-v0.2, Phi-3 mini/small/medium, DeepSeek-Math-7B, Mistral Large
low_dose_frontier_quality: good — fine 1e-4 grid resolves gradual decline; honest models degrade monotonically
near_collapse_behaviour: authors cap sweep at sigma=0.01 because output becomes incoherent above it; collapse boundary identified but not itself characterised
notes: The single best-matched dial precedent: additive Gaussian noise on all weights with a fine sigma grid on 7-8B instruct models, 5 seeds per point, reporting stable low-variance degradation curves. Also documents a real failure mode for closed-loop control: models that were underperforming can IMPROVE under noise (improvement ratios up to 10.3x).

title: Distillation Robustifies Unlearning
knob_name: alpha mixing coefficient (primary) and beta noise scale in theta' = (1-alpha)theta + alpha*beta*N with N ~ Xavier init; alpha swept 0.1-0.8, beta in {0.05,0.1,0.5,1.0}
base_model: Gemma-2 scaled variants (100M language, 300M arithmetic), Gemma-2-2B for WMDP
forget_metric: WMDP / synthetic forget-task accuracy, relearning attack robustness
low_dose_frontier_quality: good — alpha swept at 11 points 0.1-0.8, monotone tradeoff of damage vs recovery cost
near_collapse_behaviour: alpha near 0.8 destroys the model; alpha=0.6/beta=0.1 already near-oracle damage; recovery via distillation restores utility
notes: Directly relevant parameterisation: interpolate toward noise rather than add unbounded noise, so the dial is bounded in [0,1] and cannot diverge. Reports alpha dominates beta as the effective knob (a 1-D control variable). Also the only source here combining a noise dial with a repair stage.

title: Analog Foundation Models
knob_name: per-channel additive Gaussian noise, magnitude = gamma * max(|W_:,i|), swept 0-10% of per-channel max
low_dose_frontier_quality: excellent — full 0-10% sweep, smooth monotone decline, two models
near_collapse_behaviour: graceful decline out to 10% of per-channel max; no cliff observed inside the swept range (off-the-shelf models lose ~8-10% avg accuracy at hardware-realistic noise)
notes: Best published smooth monotone weight-noise dose-response curve at ~1-4B scale. Key transferable design choice: scale sigma per output channel by max|W| rather than globally, which keeps the dose comparable across layers of very different weight scale — exactly what per-checkpoint calibration needs. Noise-aware finetuning flattens the curve (i.e. the model can be made MORE noise-tolerant, a hazard for a 30-day schedule if any healing is applied).

title: Noise Injection Systemically Degrades Large Language Model Safety Guardrails
knob_name: sigma of N(0,sigma^2) added to every activation tensor via forward pre-hooks
base_model: Gemma 2B/7B, Gemma-2 2B/9B/27B, Llama-3/3.1-8B, Qwen2/2.5-7B, Mistral-7B, Yi-1.5-6B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B
low_dose_frontier_quality: moderate — per-model usable sigma bands reported but coarse
near_collapse_behaviour: usable sigma bands are narrow and model-specific (Gemma-2B 0.10-0.20 vs Qwen2 0.002-0.0035, ~50x spread); above band output stops being coherent
notes: Best evidence on WHICH capability falls first: under activation noise, safety/refusal behaviour degrades well before chain-of-thought reasoning (harmful rate 5%->31.4% on Gemma-2B, 2%->32% on Llama-3, while CoT stays largely intact). Also the cleanest warning that activation noise has a very model-specific and narrow operating band, so it is a worse control variable than weight noise despite being cheaper.

title: The Unreasonable Ineffectiveness of the Deeper Layers
low_dose_frontier_quality: poor for fine control — one layer of a 34-layer model is a ~3% step
near_collapse_behaviour: explicit CLIFF: QA accuracy is flat then transitions to random guessing (25% MMLU) at 20-55% layers dropped depending on model (Qwen ~20%, Phi-2 ~25%, Mistral ~35%, Llama-2-13B/70B 45-55%)
notes: The definitive cliff paper. Two decoupled degradation modes matter for us: next-token loss degrades smoothly and continuously with layers dropped, while QA/MMLU sits flat and then falls off a cliff. Healing with QLoRA restores the smooth loss curve and pushes the QA cliff slightly later. Implication: layer removal is unsuitable as the primary dial for a precommitted daily curve, but is a plausible day-27-to-30 terminal-collapse instrument precisely because it produces a cliff.

title: ShortGPT: Layers in Large Language Models are More Redundant Than You Expect
knob_name: number of layers deleted by Block Influence score
low_dose_frontier_quality: poor — coarse discrete steps; layer ordering by BI is fixed per checkpoint
near_collapse_behaviour: sharp drop: MMLU falls steeply past a specific layer count (Fig 5) rather than declining gradually
notes: Numbers: Llama-2-7B 27.1% layers removed -> MMLU 45.39 to 43.96, 95.69% of dense average retained; Llama-2-13B 24.6% removed -> MMLU 55.00 to 54.69, 97.34% retained; Baichuan2-13B 24.7% removed -> MMLU 59.50 to 52.11, 87.33% retained. Useful mainly as a scheduling insight: BI gives a principled ORDER in which to remove layers, so a per-day 'one more layer' schedule is at least reproducible.

title: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models
low_dose_frontier_quality: good in 0-50% band (ppl 5.68 -> 7.26 on LLaMA-7B), very fine-grained knob
near_collapse_behaviour: collapse between 60% and 80%: at 80% unstructured the best SparseGPT result is 25.86 on LLaMA-2-70B vs 3.12 dense; magnitude pruning goes NaN
notes: Digitised 50% unstructured sparsity WikiText ppl (dense / magnitude / SparseGPT / Wanda): LLaMA-7B 5.68/17.29/7.22/7.26; 13B 5.09/20.21/6.21/6.15; 30B 4.77/7.54/5.31/5.24; 65B 3.56/5.90/4.57/4.57; LLaMA-2-7B 5.12/14.89/6.51/6.42; 2-13B 4.57/6.37/5.63/5.56; 2-70B 3.12/4.98/3.98/3.98. Magnitude pruning (the cheapest variant) degrades much faster than calibrated pruning — for an art piece that is an argument FOR magnitude pruning as an expressive dial.

title: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can Be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot
low_dose_frontier_quality: good but requires a calibration pass per dose
near_collapse_behaviour: 60% sparsity still near-lossless on 175B models; degradation accelerates sharply beyond; small models degrade far earlier than large ones
notes: Included as the calibrated-pruning reference point and as the scale caveat: all headline 'graceful' pruning numbers are for 7B-175B models. A 4B model sits at the fragile end of the scale trend, so our sparsity budget will be smaller and the collapse knee earlier than these papers suggest.

title: SliceGPT: Compress Large Language Models by Deleting Rows and Columns
low_dose_frontier_quality: good — percentage slicing is a near-continuous structural knob with a per-percent perplexity curve
near_collapse_behaviour: Llama-2-70B: dense ppl 3.32, 25% sliced 4.60, 30% sliced 5.05; >30% retains under 90% of zero-shot performance; smaller models (Phi-2 2.7B) degrade markedly faster at the same slice %
notes: The most controllable structural dial found: slicing % behaves like a continuous variable (unlike whole-layer removal) and has a published per-percent curve. Requires a PCA/calibration pass per dose and changes tensor shapes, so it is not re-drawable on a copy as cheaply as noise. Note Phi-2 at 2.7B retains only ~90% at 25% slicing vs 99% for Llama-2-70B — the small-model penalty again.

title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
low_dose_frontier_quality: very poor — only 3-4 usable dose levels (16/8/4/3 bit), and 16->4 bit is nearly free
near_collapse_behaviour: cliff at 3-bit and below for naive RTN (OPT-175B 8.34 -> 7.3e3; BLOOM-176B 8.11 -> 571); GPTQ softens it (8.68 / 8.64) but 2-bit collapses
notes: Digitised: OPT-175B WikiText2 FP16 8.34, GPTQ 4-bit 8.37, GPTQ 3-bit 8.68, RTN 3-bit 7.3e3. Small models are much worse: OPT-125M GPTQ 3-bit 53.85, OPT-350M 33.79, OPT-1.3B 20.97 vs OPT-175B 8.68. Verdict for us: bit-width is too coarse and too scale-sensitive to be a 30-step dial, but naive RTN at 3-bit is an excellent one-shot terminal-collapse instrument.

title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
near_collapse_behaviour: phase transition at ~6.7B: naive int8 goes from fine to catastrophic (13B: 12.45 fp32 -> 19.08 absmax int8); removing ~0.1% outlier dims degrades perplexity by 600-1000% while removing random dims changes it by 0.1%
notes: Most useful finding for dial design: damage is dominated by a tiny number of outlier feature dimensions. Uniform Gaussian weight noise mostly misses them (random dims are near-harmless), which is exactly why uniform noise degrades smoothly — and it suggests a deliberately expressive late-stage dial: perturb only the outlier channels to get large damage from a small dose.

title: Accuracy is Not All You Need
utility_metric: accuracy, flips (% answers changed vs baseline), KL divergence, distance metrics
notes: Load-bearing for our measurement layer, not a dial. Aggregate accuracy is nearly blind to real behavioural change: across 7 tasks accuracy moved <=2% while flips ranged 0.26%-13.62% (Llama-2-70B MMLU: BnB W8A8 -0.55% acc / 3.32% flips; BnB W4A4 -0.78% / 5.65%; GPTQ W8A16 -0.01% / 0.26%). If the closed loop is controlled purely on benchmark accuracy it will under-read early damage; flips (or KL vs the day-0 model) is a far more sensitive low-dose control signal — important for days 1-22 where the daily step is only ~1%.

title: Model Hemorrhage and the Robustness Limits of Large Language Models
near_collapse_behaviour: reports robustness THRESHOLDS: structured pruning collapses near 50% sparsity; unstructured stable below 60%; quantisation degradation turns from linear to exponential below 3-bit; Llama-2-70B keeps high MMLU after 40% layers pruned
notes: Useful as a cross-dial map of where each knob's knee sits, and it names the phenomenon we are deliberately inducing. Survey-level: thresholds are quoted rather than freshly swept, so treat as orientation, not as calibration data.

title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
low_dose_frontier_quality: slow at first: gen 0 ppl ~20 rising to ~28 by gen 1 without data preservation; keeping 10% real data keeps degradation minor across 9 generations
near_collapse_behaviour: late generations lose distribution tails then variance; by gen 7-9 outputs become repetitive phrase loops rather than noise
notes: Different mechanism from our dial (data-loop, not parameter perturbation) and demonstrated only at 125M. Its value is aesthetic and terminal: it produces a specific, legible failure signature (repetition, tail loss, collapse to the mode) that reads as senility rather than as static — a strong candidate for the day 28-30 aesthetic if Gaussian noise's terminal signature turns out to be uninterestingly garbled. Cost: a fine-tuning loop per generation, which is heavier than re-drawing noise.

title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences
notes: The control-law precedent we should copy. Exact rule: e_t = clip((KL(pi_t,rho) - KL_target)/KL_target, -0.2, 0.2); beta_{t+1} = beta_t * (1 + K_beta * e_t), with K_beta = 0.1 and KL_target 6-10 nats. This is a multiplicative proportional controller with a clipped relative error — directly transplantable to 'measured decline vs today's target decline' driving log(sigma). The clip is the important part: it bounds how far one day's dose can jump.

title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
low_dose_frontier_quality: good — lambda swept on a 0.0-1.0 grid in 0.05/0.1 steps with a documented selection rule (largest lambda retaining 95% control performance)
near_collapse_behaviour: not characterised at extreme lambda; the published protocol deliberately stops before the model breaks
notes: An alternative continuous dial that is deterministic rather than stochastic: move the weights along a fixed direction with a scalar lambda. GPT-2 toxicity: 4.8% -> 0.8% toxic generations, toxicity score 0.06 -> 0.01, WikiText-103 ppl 16.4 -> 16.9. Attractive as a *steerable* decay (choose the direction of decline — e.g. negate a 'coherent assistant' vector) and as a per-day reproducible step, but it needs a fine-tuned endpoint to define the direction, unlike noise which needs nothing.

title: The Truth is in There: Improving Reasoning in Language Models with Layer-Selective Rank Reduction
low_dose_frontier_quality: BAD — non-monotone: removing higher-order components can INCREASE accuracy (GPT-J CounterFact 13.3% -> 24.1%)
near_collapse_behaviour: not characterised; the interesting region is the improvement region, not collapse
notes: The explicit monotonicity counterexample and the reason we must verify monotonicity per checkpoint rather than assume it. A damage dial that sometimes helps is unusable open-loop; it also means any single-day accuracy INCREASE in our closed loop is a plausible artefact, not a measurement error, and the controller must not over-correct for it.

title: PrisonBreak: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with at Most Twenty-Five Targeted Bit-flips
utility_metric: attack success rate, benign task accuracy
low_dose_frontier_quality: unusable as a graded dial — 5-25 flips out of billions changes behaviour drastically with minimal utility change
near_collapse_behaviour: extreme cliff: arbitrary (untargeted) bit flips drive decoding to NaN within a few flips
notes: Included as the boundary case that defines what NOT to use. It also makes a design point that matters artistically: parameter damage can be made either behaviourally targeted (safety only) or globally catastrophic (NaN) depending on WHERE it lands, with almost no middle ground in the discrete regime. Continuous dense noise is the opposite: it averages over locations and therefore behaves smoothly.
